name: Terrain Tile Source Nodes
description: The PURE half of the terrain serving lane: it decodes source DEM GeoTIFF granules into quantized-mesh-1.0 tiles wrapped in $DTT records, and renders the tileset's layer.json, and does nothing else. capabilities [], browser + wasmedge, request-scoped, no state between invocations. Every DEM byte it decodes was fetched by com.digitalarsenal.hostcap.http-request and every record it emits is persisted downstream; scheduling and pyramid orchestration live in the sibling terrain-ingest module, exactly as geonames-source / geonames-ingest are split. The source granules are DEFLATE-compressed Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs and there is no host inflate capability (and none may be added), so miniz 3.1.2 is vendored under vendor/miniz-3.1.2 (MIT, SHA-256 pinned and re-verified on every build) - the same vendored copy geonames-source and cell-tower-source use. A minimal little-endian TIFF/BigTIFF reader (tiled or strip layout, DEFLATE via tinfl, predictor 1 and floating-point predictor 3) lives in-guest for the same reason. Heights are redistributed on the source dataset's own vertical datum (a geoid), stated verbatim in VERTICAL_DATUM/VERTICAL_DATUM_NAME, never silently converted.

sequentialJustification.detail: Both methods are single-pass transforms over the frames the flow hands them: decode the DEM granules covering one output tile and encode one quantized mesh, or render one layer.json body. Tiles are processed one at a time, there is no shared mutable state, no worker pool and no fan-out inside the guest, so it compiles single-thread rather than claiming a wasi-threads contract it does not honour.

methods.displayName: Encode one quantized-mesh terrain tile from source DEM granules

acceptedTypeSets.description: The tile plan from terrain-ingest: tileset identity, z/x/y address, grid size, water-mask directive, pyramid limits, and the dataset provenance every record must be published under.

wildcardJustification.detail: Intra-flow control frame produced and consumed inside this flow; its shape is defined by the sibling terrain-ingest node, not by SDS.

inputPorts.description: The tile plan carrying the address, grid size and dataset contract.

acceptedTypeSets.description: hostcap/http-request responses carrying the source DEM GeoTIFF granules intersecting the requested tile. A 404 is a granule the dataset does not publish (open ocean), which is data, not an error.

wildcardJustification.detail: Intra-flow control frame produced and consumed inside this flow; its shape is defined by the host op that feeds it, not by SDS.

inputPorts.description: One response frame per 1x1-degree source granule intersecting the tile; a tile corner-spanning four granules needs four.

acceptedTypeSets.description: Size-prefixed $DTT FlatBuffer record stream: one Digital Terrain Tile per invocation, quantized-mesh payload inline.
Encode summary: sample counts, no-data counts, coverage fraction, height range, payload sizes and the vertical-datum note.

wildcardJustification.detail: Intra-flow control frame produced and consumed inside this flow; its shape is defined by the sibling node it feeds, not by SDS.

methods.description: Decodes the DEM GeoTIFF granules intersecting one z/x/y address of the GEOGRAPHIC_WGS84 pyramid (two root tiles, TMS row origin south), samples a gridSize x gridSize post lattice bilinearly, and encodes one quantized-mesh-1.0 tile: ECEF header with bounding sphere and horizon occlusion point, zigzag-delta 16-bit vertex arrays, high-water-mark index encoding, edge index lists, and the watermask extension (id 2). The tile bytes ride INLINE in DTTPayloadRef.BYTES (gzip via the vendored deflate, CONTENT_ENCODING "gzip"), which is within the small-block inline allowance; the CID lane is the growth path. HEIGHTS ARE NOT CONVERTED: the source dataset publishes geoid-referenced heights and the record states VERTICAL_DATUM GEOID with the model named verbatim - a consumer that renders them as ellipsoidal accepts a stated, bounded error and the record and report both say so. A granule the dataset does not publish (HTTP 404, open ocean) decodes to height 0 with WATER_MASK_KIND UNIFORM_WATER unless the plan states otherwise; the source NO_DATA value (-32767) decodes to 0 and is counted in DATA_COVERAGE_FRACTION rather than hidden. A plan that cannot state the dataset identity, epoch, retrieval time and licence is REFUSED, never defaulted. BATCHING: the plan port is single-stream and the dem port carries at most the four corner granules, ENFORCED IN CODE; maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely declarative in the compiled flow runtime, which drains a node's queue port-blind, so any surplus is refused with error code "batched-input-frames" rather than silently destroyed.

acceptedTypeSets.description: The tileset plan from terrain-ingest: tilesetId, maxzoom, and the available-tile ranges.

wildcardJustification.detail: Intra-flow control frame produced and consumed inside this flow; its shape is defined by the sibling terrain-ingest node, not by SDS.

inputPorts.description: The tileset plan carrying maxzoom and availability.

acceptedTypeSets.description: Canonical WASM-served HTTP response envelope ($HTR, module-sdk schemas/HttpResponseAbi.fbs): STATUS 200, content-type application/json, the layer.json body inline. The host streams it back verbatim.

outputPorts.description: Exactly one HTTP response envelope carrying the complete layer.json body.

methods.description: Renders the complete layer.json body for a quantized-mesh-1.0 tileset - tilejson 2.1.0, format quantized-mesh-1.0, scheme tms, projection EPSG:4326, bounds [-180,-90,180,90], minzoom 0, the plan's maxzoom, extensions ["watermask"] (octvertexnormals is omitted until normals ship), and the plan's available ranges passed through VERBATIM - and emits it as the SDK's canonical $HTR HttpResponse envelope with the body inline, never as a JSON control frame. The availability index is the orchestrator's knowledge, not this encoder's, so it is never synthesized here. BATCHING: single-stream by contract, enforced in code; a surplus is refused with error code "batched-input-frames".
